title: URecJPQ: Memory-efficient Multimodal Recommendation Models through RecJPQ in Large-Scale Scenarios
summary: Training state-of-the-art recommendation models on large-scale industrial datasets can be a challenging task due to the high number of users and items which are typically represented through ID embeddings. Such embeddings typically require a large amount of memory resources, which are not always available. This problem is further exacerbated in multimodal recommendation, in which multimodal item features generally improve recommendation performance, but require more resources to encode. In this paper, we introduce URecJPQ, a Joint Product Quantization method specifically designed for large-scale and multimodal top-k recommendation tasks, in which the vast number of users and items, combined with the available modalities, further increases the memory demands for the computation. The core idea is to represent each user/item not as a fully learned, unique embedding, but rather as a concatenation of shared learned sub-embeddings, thereby significantly reducing the total number of trainable parameters. Our experiments on three widely-used datasets across different domains (movies, baby and sports products) show that URecJPQ can be effectively applied to multimodal recommendation settings. In large scale scenarios, we observe a substantial reduction in checkpoint sizes and the number of trainable parameters (ranging from 86% to 98%, and 98% to 99%, respectively), with only a marginal decrease in accuracy (8.5% on recall and 16% on NDCG, on average), and, in some cases, even performance improvements (up to 85%), as in the baby products domain. Our codebase is available at https://anonymous.4open.science/r/large_mmrecjpq-839B/README.md.

AI.tldr: This paper proposes URecJPQ, a memory-efficient Joint Product Quantization method for large-scale multimodal recommendation, which drastically reduces trainable parameters and model size with only small average accuracy drops, and even achieves performance gains in some domains.
AI.motivation: Training state-of-the-art large-scale recommendation models requires huge memory for ID embeddings of massive users and items; this memory issue becomes even worse for multimodal recommendation, since additional multimodal features increase resource demands, which is not feasible when memory resources are limited.
AI.method: Proposes URecJPQ, a Joint Product Quantization method for large-scale multimodal top-k recommendation. Instead of using fully learned unique embeddings for each user/item, it represents each embedding as a concatenation of shared learned sub-embeddings, which reduces the total number of trainable parameters significantly.
AI.result: Experiments on three public datasets from different domains show that URecJPQ reduces checkpoint size by 86% to 98% and trainable parameters by 98% to 99% in large-scale scenarios, with only an average marginal accuracy decrease (8.5% for recall, 16% for NDCG), and delivers up to 85% performance improvement in the baby products domain.
AI.conclusion: URecJPQ can effectively reduce memory consumption of large-scale multimodal recommendation models with only minor average accuracy loss, and can even improve performance in some cases, making it suitable for large-scale scenarios.

title: LLM-as-a-Judge for Reliable and Explainable Offline Evaluation in Top-K Recommendation
summary:
Recommendation evaluation plays a crucial role in guiding the refinement and deployment of recommender systems. Most existing trials rely on offline evaluation using Top-K metrics computed over holdout user behaviors. However, we identify two fundamental limitations that undermine their ability to deliver reliable and explainable evaluations. Regarding reliability, offline evaluation treats observed user feedback as a proxy of true preferences and enforces rigid ID matching between the proxy and recommendation. In practice, feedback collections are inherently shaped by incomplete and biased item exposure, leading to distorted and unreliable assessments. Regarding explainability, Top-K metrics only establish numerical scores without offering meaningful insights to support them, thereby reinforcing the black-box nature of offline evaluation.
  In this paper, we propose a reliable and explainable LLM-as-a-Judge framework for offline recommendation evaluation. To enhance reliability, we introduce a semantic proxy from user textual behaviors to represent their true preferences. This proxy allows for more flexible matching between preferences and recommendations in the semantic space, rather than depending on the holdout feedback. To ensure explainability, the LLM Judge adopts a reasoning-then-scoring process to generate relevance judgments along with explicit rationale. Finally, we aggregate the individual scores into global Top-K metrics to quantify overall recommendation quality, and provide justification for each preference hit or miss. Extensive experiments demonstrate that the LLM Judge achieves solid reliability, explainability, and robustness in evaluation.

AI.tldr: 本文提出了一个用于Top-K推荐离线评估的LLM-as-a-Judge框架，解决了传统离线评估可靠性不足和缺乏可解释性的问题，通过实验验证了该框架在评估中具备良好的可靠性、可解释性和鲁棒性。
AI.motivation: 传统基于留存用户行为的Top-K离线推荐评估存在两个核心缺陷：可靠性方面，将观测用户反馈作为真实偏好的代理，要求代理和推荐严格ID匹配，但反馈收集受到不完整和有偏的项目曝光影响，导致评估结果失真不可靠；可解释性方面，Top-K指标仅提供数值分数，无法给出有意义的支撑见解，让离线评估成为黑箱。因此需要新的评估方法解决这些问题。
AI.method: 提出LLM-as-a-Judge评估框架：1. 为提升可靠性，从用户文本行为构建语义偏好代理，在语义空间实现偏好和推荐的灵活匹配，不再依赖留存反馈；2. 为保证可解释性，LLM Judge采用先推理后评分的流程，生成相关性判断同时输出明确推理依据；3. 最后聚合个体得分得到全局Top-K指标，同时为每个偏好命中/未命中提供解释。
AI.result: 大量实验结果表明，所提出的LLM Judge框架在推荐离线评估中，具备出色的可靠性、可解释性和鲁棒性。
AI.conclusion: 所提LLM-as-a-Judge框架能够为Top-K推荐提供可靠且可解释的离线评估，解决了传统离线评估方法的核心缺陷。

AI.production_deployment: 摘要未提及该方法是否有实际生产部署、线上A/B测试或工业落地，仅开展了离线实验。

title: Who Owns the AI Recommendation? A Multi-Industry Empirical Map of Brand Category Ownership Across Large Language Models
summary: Large language models now mediate how buyers discover products and services, making the competitive structure of AI-generated recommendations a strategic concern for brands. A basic question has lacked large-scale empirical answers: in a given category, which brand does a model recommend, and how concentrated is that ownership? Across 3,750 responses spanning 50 brands, five industries, and 250 brand-free category queries on three models (GPT-5.2, Google Gemini 3 Flash, and Perplexity sonar-pro), each query repeated five times under a dice-roll stability protocol, we propose three exploratory metrics: the Category Ownership Index (COI), a brand's share of mentions within a category; the Competitive Vacuum Index (CVI), flagging categories with no single leader; and the Displacement Score (DS), quantifying asymmetric substitution between brand pairs. In this sample, recommendation concentration was moderate: the mean Gini coefficient was 0.28 (95% CI [0.16, 0.41]), below the 0.60 power-law threshold we set. Competitive vacuums were rare, appearing in 8.0% of queries, so the models named at least one sampled brand in most cases. Cross-model agreement on the top-recommended brand was 41.6%: a top position on one model did not reliably hold on another. Displacement was industry-dependent, from co-recommendation in consulting (0.4:1) to one-directional substitution up to 4.3:1, with an unweighted mean of 2.4:1 across the five industries. A BERTopic check placed only 4.2% of discovered topic clusters outside the original categories. Within the scope studied, these results sit in tension with a strong winner-takes-all narrative around AI recommendation, and the three metrics offer a candidate, reproducible procedure for competitive-intelligence analysis that future work can validate.
comment: 21 pages, 4 figures, 7 tables. Under review at Journal of Marketing Analytics (Palgrave Macmillan). Data and analysis code on Zenodo, https://doi.org/10.5281/zenodo.20788142

AI.tldr: This paper conducts a large-scale empirical study on brand ownership of AI-generated product/service recommendations across three major large language models (LLMs), proposes three metrics for measuring recommendation concentration and brand competition, and finds moderate concentration that contradicts the strong winner-takes-all narrative.
AI.motivation: LLMs increasingly mediate buyers' product/service discovery, making the competitive structure of AI-generated recommendations a key strategic concern for brands, but there is a lack of large-scale empirical answers to which brands LLMs recommend most in a category and how concentrated recommendation ownership is.
AI.method: The study collected 3,750 responses across 50 brands, 5 industries, 250 brand-free category queries on 3 LLMs (GPT-5.2, Google Gemini 3 Flash, Perplexity sonar-pro), with each query repeated 5 times under a stability protocol. Three exploratory metrics are proposed: Category Ownership Index (COI), Competitive Vacuum Index (CVI), and Displacement Score (DS) to measure brand share, competitive vacuums, and asymmetric brand substitution respectively.
AI.result: The results show that recommendation concentration is moderate with a mean Gini coefficient of 0.28, below the 0.60 power-law threshold. Competitive vacuums are rare (only 8.0% of queries). Cross-model agreement on the top-recommended brand is only 41.6%, meaning top positions are not consistent across models. Asymmetric displacement is industry-dependent, ranging from 0.4:1 in consulting to 4.3:1 with a mean of 2.4:1. Only 4.2% of topic clusters are outside original categories, indicating good category alignment.
AI.conclusion: The findings contradict the strong winner-takes-all narrative for AI recommendation within the studied scope. The three proposed metrics provide a reproducible procedure for competitive intelligence analysis that can be validated by future work.

title: The Language Blind Spot: How Query Language and Brand Recognition Tier Shape AI-Constructed Brand Reputation Across Twelve European Languages
summary: Large language models (LLMs) increasingly mediate how people form impressions of organisations, yet most monitoring is done in English, assuming an English query returns a representative picture. We measure how far that holds. We queried three grounded LLMs (GPT-5.4, Gemini 3.1 Pro, Perplexity Sonar Pro) about 66 brands from eleven Northern, Baltic, and Central European markets, in twelve languages across four families (Germanic, Uralic, Baltic, Slavic), generating 35,640 responses. Multilingual embeddings (BGE-M3) allow cross-language comparison without translation. Three results emerge. First, AI-constructed reputation is language-bound: mean cross-language cosine similarity is 0.825, same-family responses are more similar than cross-family (0.844 vs 0.820; d = 0.31), and sentiment varies by language (F = 268.5, eta^2 = 0.077), with Uralic and Baltic languages most positive and Germanic, including English, most critical; clustering recovers the Slavic and Baltic families (cophenetic 0.915). Second, query language shifts which brands are recommended far more than how they are described: moving from an English query to a brand's home language raises recommendation share by 0.80 for local champions but only 0.15 for global multinationals (t = -8.84, p < 0.001), with no comparable reversal in sentiment. An English-only audit therefore understates a local champion's AI visibility. Third, response stability varies more with model choice than with language (eta^2_model = 0.32 vs eta^2_language = 0.01, on a five-iteration replication over a 20-brand subset). These results indicate that English-only AI reputation monitoring leaves a measurable language blind spot, concentrated in the visibility of locally headquartered brands.
comment: 17 pages, 3 figures. Data and analysis code on Zenodo, https://doi.org/10.5281/zenodo.20794390

AI.tldr: This paper investigates the "language blind spot" in AI-constructed brand reputation, measuring how query language and brand type affect LLM-generated reputation results across 12 European languages, and finds that English-only monitoring creates bias especially for local brands.
AI.motivation: Large language models increasingly mediate people's impressions of organizations, but most current AI brand reputation monitoring is done only in English, assuming English queries can yield representative results, which has not been empirically tested across multiple languages.
AI.method: Three grounded LLMs (GPT-5.4, Gemini 3.1 Pro, Perplexity Sonar Pro) were queried about 66 brands from 11 European markets in 12 languages from 4 language families, generating 35,640 responses. Multilingual BGE-M3 embeddings were used for cross-language comparison without translation, and statistical analysis was conducted to compare similarity, sentiment, recommendation share, and response stability across languages and brand types.
AI.result: 1. AI-constructed brand reputation is language-dependent: cross-language cosine similarity is 0.825, same-language family responses are more similar than cross-family, sentiment varies significantly by language with Uralic/Baltic languages being most positive and Germanic (including English) most critical. 2. Query language affects which brands are recommended far more than sentiment description: switching from English to a brand's home language increases recommendation share by 0.80 for local champions vs only 0.15 for global multinationals. 3. Response stability is affected more by model choice (eta^2=0.32) than language (eta^2=0.01).
AI.conclusion: English-only AI brand reputation monitoring leaves a measurable language blind spot, which is particularly concentrated in the underrepresentation of visibility of locally headquartered brands.

title: Towards Fast Domain Adaptation and Fine-Grained User Simulation for Evaluating Conversational Recommender Systems
summary: Conversational Recommender Systems (CRSs) enhance user experience through multi-turn interactions, yet evaluating their performance remains challenging. While Large Language Model (LLM) based user simulators are effective, they suffer from three key limitations: (1) Lack of Domain Adaptability: Reliance on fixed prompts and predefined action spaces hinders transfer to novel domains; (2) Limited User Modeling: Inability to accurately replicate subtle linguistic styles and dynamic preferences; (3) Insufficient Evaluation Validity: Existing simulators fail to adequately assess fundamental capabilities and system robustness. To overcome these, we propose AdaptSim, an Adaptive domain and automatic prompt tuning User Simulator. AdaptSim offers an efficient framework for evaluating CRSs by enabling realistic behavior modeling and diverse style generation. It leverages automatic prompt generation and an open action mechanism to reduce manual effort and improve cross-domain flexibility. For response generation, we employ controlled text generation with a "think-then-respond" strategy for fine-grained control over language style. For CRS evaluation, AdaptSim incorporates a novel Breadth-First Search (BFS)-based, turn-level pairwise comparison framework for comprehensive assessment. Extensive experiments across three domains and four LLMs demonstrate that AdaptSim generates realistic dialogues, enabling a highly effective and reliable evaluation of CRS capabilities and robustness.

AI.tldr: 本文针对对话推荐系统（CRS）评估中基于大语言模型的用户模拟器存在的领域适应性差、用户建模粗糙、评估有效性不足的问题，提出了自适应领域和自动提示调优的用户模拟器AdaptSim，实验证明它能生成真实对话，有效可靠评估CRS的能力和鲁棒性。
AI.motivation: 对话推荐系统的性能评估一直存在挑战，虽然基于大语言模型的用户模拟器已被证明有效，但仍存在三个关键缺陷：一是缺乏领域适应性，依赖固定提示和预定义动作空间阻碍了向新领域迁移；二是用户建模能力有限，无法精准复现细微语言风格和动态偏好；三是评估有效性不足，现有模拟器无法充分评估CRS的基础能力和系统鲁棒性，因此需要提出新的用户模拟器解决这些问题。
AI.method: 提出自适应领域和自动提示调优的用户模拟器AdaptSim：1. 利用自动提示生成和开放动作机制减少人工成本，提升跨领域灵活性；2. 在响应生成上，采用带有"思考-再响应"策略的可控文本生成，实现对语言风格的细粒度控制；3. 在CRS评估上，引入了新型基于广度优先搜索（BFS）的回合级 pairwise 比较框架实现全面评估。
AI.result: 在三个领域、四个大语言模型上开展的大量实验表明，AdaptSim能够生成真实符合用户特征的对话，能够对对话推荐系统的能力和鲁棒性实现高效可靠的评估。
AI.conclusion: AdaptSim解决了现有基于LLM的用户模拟器的三大缺陷，实现了快速领域适应和细粒度用户模拟，能够有效提升对话推荐系统评估的有效性和可靠性。
